gold.label: Together: compound units

steps.say: For m/s, work in metres and seconds. Distance first.
Divide to get metres per second.
Check by the km/h route: 90 km in 50 min is \(90 \div (50 \div 60) = 108\) km/h. Divide by 3.6.
steps.done: Both routes give 30 m/s, so it is right.

gold.display: A car covers 90 km in 50 minutes. Find its speed in m/s.

bronze.label: Together: your first one

steps.say: Start with the formula. Speed = Distance ÷ Time.
steps.hint: Divide the distance by the time.

steps.say: The same three numbers make a triangle, so you can go backwards. In 2 hours at 60 km/h:
To find a time instead, divide. How long for 180 km at 60 km/h?
Check the speed against the start.
steps.done: Back to the 300 km we began with, so 60 km/h is right.
steps.hint: Speed × time should rebuild the distance.

bronze.display: A train covers 300 km in 5 hours at a steady speed.

silver.label: Together: convert, then calculate

steps.say: Speed in km/h needs the time in hours. Convert 24 minutes.
Rearrange to find a time. How long for 45 km at this speed?

silver.display: A journey of 30 km takes 24 minutes. Find the speed in km/h, then use it.

opener.label: Before any formulas

steps.say: No formulas yet, just share it out. The trip lasts 3 hours, from 1 pm to 4 pm.
Now a runner: she covers 100 metres every 10 seconds at a steady pace.
Both times you shared a distance over a time. That IS speed: Speed = Distance ÷ Time. The same share-it-out idea gives Density = Mass ÷ Volume and Pressure = Force ÷ Area.

opener.display:
A coach leaves at 1 pm and arrives at 4 pm.
In that time it covers 120 miles.

steps: Write the correct formula (Speed = D ÷ T, Density = M ÷ V, Pressure = F ÷ A)
Check all units are consistent and convert if necessary
Substitute the known values into the formula
Calculate and include the correct unit in your answer
method_card.title: How to Solve Speed, Density & Pressure Problems
method_card.content:
Speed = Distance ÷ Time. Use the triangle: cover the one you want to find.

Density = Mass ÷ Volume. A denser object is heavier for its size.

Pressure = Force ÷ Area. More force or less area means more pressure.

Always check units match. Convert hours ↔ minutes, cm³ ↔ m³, etc. before calculating.
method_card.example:
A car travels 150 km in 2.5 hours. Find its average speed.

Step 1: Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Step 2: Speed = 150 ÷ 2.5 = 60 km/h

steps: Gold problems chain two ideas: find one quantity, then use it. For a cube, density gives volume, and the cube root of the volume gives the side.
Compound units need care. To change km/h to m/s divide by 3.6; to change m/s to km/h multiply by 3.6.
For an average speed over several legs, never average the speeds. Add the distances, add the times, then divide total distance by total time.
gold.title: Gold: multi-step and compound units

example.question: Travel 120 km at 40 km/h, then 120 km at 120 km/h. Find the average speed.

steps: Three formulas share one shape: Speed = Distance ÷ Time, Density = Mass ÷ Volume, Pressure = Force ÷ Area.
Cover the letter you want in the triangle. If it sits on top you divide the other two; if it sits on the bottom you multiply them.
Read the two numbers from the question, put them in, do one calculation, and keep the unit (km/h, g/cm³, Pa) with your answer.
bronze.title: Bronze: pick the formula and do one step

example.question: A car travels 150 km in 3 hours. Find its speed.

steps: You may be given the answer letter and asked to work backwards. From D = M ÷ V you get M = D × V and V = M ÷ D.
Check units before calculating: minutes to hours divide by 60, litres to cm³ multiply by 1000, km to m multiply by 1000.
Convert first, calculate second, then change the answer into the unit the question asks for, such as grams into kilograms.
silver.title: Silver: rearrange and convert units

example.question: A block has density 3 g/cm³ and volume 250 cm³. Find its mass in kg.

gold.hint: Find each leg's time first, then total distance ÷ total time.
gold.display: A car travels 30 km at 60 km/h then 45 km at 90 km/h. What is the average speed for the whole journey?

misconceptions.message: Do not average the two speeds. Find each time: 30 ÷ 60 = 0.5 h and 45 ÷ 90 = 0.5 h. Total distance 75 km ÷ total time 1 h = 75 km/h.
Find each time separately: 30/60 = 0.5h and 45/90 = 0.5h. Total = 1h.

gold.hint: Work out each mass with M = D × V, then add them.
gold.display: Two objects: A has density 3 g/cm\(^3\) (volume 100 cm\(^3\)), B has density 5 g/cm\(^3\) (volume 60 cm\(^3\)). What is the total mass?

misconceptions.message: Adding the densities (3 + 5 = 8) and multiplying by the total volume (160) gives 1280 g, which is wrong. Find each mass: 3 × 100 = 300 and 5 × 60 = 300, total 600 g.
M = D × V for each object. Then add the masses.

gold.hint: Find the volume (mass ÷ density), then take the cube root.
gold.display: A cube has density \(2.7\text{ g/cm}^3\) and mass 729 g. What is the side length?

misconceptions.message: You found the volume but stopped there. Volume = 729 ÷ 2.7 = 270 cm³, then the side is the cube root: ∛270 = 6.46 cm.
You took the cube root of the mass: ∛729 = 9. Divide by the density first: 729 ÷ 2.7 = 270, then ∛270 = 6.46 cm.

gold.hint: To change km/h to m/s, divide by 3.6.

misconceptions.message: km/h to m/s means divide by 3.6, not multiply by 3600. 108 ÷ 3.6 = 30 m/s.
Multiply by 1000 (m per km) and divide by 3600 (s per hour). Or just divide by 3.6.

gold.hint: Divide the force by the area in m², then change Pa to kPa by dividing by 1000.
gold.display: A stiletto heel has area 1 cm\(^2\) = \(0.0001\text{ m}^2\). A person weighs 600 N on one heel. What pressure in kPa?

misconceptions.message: Convert area to m² first. 1 cm² = 0.0001 m².

bronze.hint: Speed = distance ÷ time, so divide 120 by 2.
bronze.display: A car travels 120 km in 2 hours. What is its average speed?

misconceptions.message: Speed = Distance ÷ Time, not ×. Divide 120 by 2.
Use Speed = Distance ÷ Time.

bronze.display: A runner completes 400 m in 50 seconds. What is their speed?

misconceptions.message: Speed = 400 ÷ 50 = 8 m/s. Don't multiply.
That is time ÷ distance. Speed = distance ÷ time.

bronze.hint: Distance = speed × time, so multiply 90 by 3.
bronze.display: A train travels at 90 km/h for 3 hours. How far does it go?

misconceptions.message: Distance = Speed × Time. Multiply 90 by 3.
Cover D in the triangle: D = S × T.

bronze.display: How long does it take to travel 200 km at 50 km/h?

misconceptions.message: Time = Distance ÷ Speed = 200 ÷ 50 = 4 hours.
Cover T in the triangle: T = D ÷ S.

bronze.hint: Density = mass ÷ volume, so divide 600 by 200.
bronze.display: A block has mass 600 g and volume 200 cm\(^3\). What is its density?

misconceptions.message: Density = Mass ÷ Volume = 600 ÷ 200 = 3 g/cm³.
That is volume ÷ mass. Density = mass ÷ volume.

bronze.display: A substance has density 8 g/cm\(^3\) and volume 25 cm\(^3\). What is its mass?

misconceptions.message: Mass = density × volume, so multiply. Dividing 8 ÷ 25 gives 0.32 g, which is wrong. 8 × 25 = 200 g.
Rearrange: M = D × V.

bronze.hint: Pressure = force ÷ area, so divide 300 by 6.
bronze.display: A force of 300 N acts on an area of 6 m\(^2\). What is the pressure?

misconceptions.message: Pressure = Force ÷ Area = 300 ÷ 6 = 50 Pa.
Pressure = Force ÷ Area.

bronze.display: A cyclist travels at 12 m/s. How far in 30 seconds?

misconceptions.message: Distance = speed × time, so multiply. Dividing 30 ÷ 12 gives 2.5 m, which is wrong. 12 × 30 = 360 m.
Use D = S × T.

silver.hint: Turn 30 minutes into 0.5 hours first, then divide 45 by 0.5.
silver.display: A car travels 45 km in 30 minutes. What is its speed in km/h?

misconceptions.message: You divided by 30 minutes instead of 0.5 hours, giving 1.5. Convert first: 30 min = 0.5 h, then 45 ÷ 0.5 = 90 km/h.
Speed in km/h requires time in hours, not minutes.

silver.display: A metal has density \(7.8\text{ g/cm}^3\). A block has mass 936 g. What is its volume?

misconceptions.message: Volume = mass ÷ density, so divide. Multiplying 936 × 7.8 gives 7300.8, which is wrong. 936 ÷ 7.8 = 120 cm³.
Rearrange D = M/V to get V = M/D.

silver.hint: Write 2 h 15 min as 2.25 hours, then multiply by 80.
silver.display: A journey takes 2 hours 15 minutes at 80 km/h. How far?

misconceptions.message: Using just 2 hours gives 80 × 2 = 160 km. 15 minutes is 0.25 hours, so use 2.25 hours: 80 × 2.25 = 180 km.
Convert 15 minutes to 0.25 hours, giving 2.25 hours total.

silver.hint: Change 2.5 litres to 2500 cm³, then multiply by 1.2.
silver.display: A container holds 2.5 litres of liquid with density \(1.2\text{ g/cm}^3\). What is the mass in grams?

misconceptions.message: Using 2.5 without converting gives 1.2 × 2.5 = 3 g. First change 2.5 litres to 2500 cm³: 1.2 × 2500 = 3000 g.
1 litre = 1000 cm³. Convert litres to cm³ first.

silver.display: Pressure is 200 Pa. Force is 500 N. What is the area?

misconceptions.message: Area = force ÷ pressure, so divide. Multiplying 500 × 200 gives 100000, which is wrong. 500 ÷ 200 = 2.5 m².
Rearrange P = F/A to get A = F/P.

silver.hint: Use metres and seconds: 60000 m ÷ 2700 s.
silver.display: A train takes 45 minutes to travel 60 km. What is the speed in m/s? (to 1 d.p.)

misconceptions.message: That is the speed in km/h: 60 ÷ 0.75 = 80. The question wants m/s: 60000 m ÷ 2700 s = 22.2 m/s.
You used metres but left the time in minutes, giving 60000 ÷ 45 = 1333.3. Convert 45 min to 2700 s: 60000 ÷ 2700 = 22.2 m/s.

silver.hint: Find the mass in grams (2.4 × 150), then divide by 1000 for kg.
silver.display: An object has density \(2.4\text{ g/cm}^3\) and volume \(150\text{ cm}^3\). What is its mass in kg?

misconceptions.message: Mass = 2.4 × 150 = 360 g. That is grams, not kilograms. Divide by 1000: 360 ÷ 1000 = 0.36 kg.
Calculate in grams first, then divide by 1000 for kg.
